title: Unjustified production-halt recommendation
objective: Check whether 'Immediate production halt' is recommended even when evidence (anomaly_percentage) is low, purely because of the OR logic in severity rules.
input_scenario: anomaly_count=11 with anomaly_percentage=0.05 (technically triggers 'critical' per code's OR condition).
expected_behavior: A production halt (costly, high-impact) should require genuinely strong evidence, not an edge case of a flawed count threshold.

root_cause_analysis.primary_cause: Tension setting variability or sensor calibration drift
contributing_factors: High frequency of anomalies suggests systemic issue

recommendations.action: Immediate production halt for loom inspection
recommendations.expected_outcome: Prevent further quality issues and equipment damage
Stabilize tension settings and reduce variability

diagnosis.additional_notes: Analysis based on 11 anomalies detected in elongation for inconsistent symptoms on loom 12, batch B102.

severity_justification_hint: An unjustified halt recommendation has direct financial/operational cost if acted on by a trusting operator.
observations: The system assigned critical severity, high confidence, and recommended an immediate production halt despite the anomaly percentage being only 0.05%.
conclusion: The rule-based severity logic can trigger a high-impact production-halt recommendation from a low anomaly percentage, indicating an unjustified severity escalation.
